text:
ops-bot: Release train bulletin — small policy update + upcoming migration schedule. Read before planning rollouts this sprint. :information_source:

sylvia: Heads-up: we're changing the canary concurrency rule across regions. Effective immediately: max 2 concurrent canaries per region for the next 6 weeks while we run the quant-kernel migration. This is to reduce scheduling churn while infra shifts nodes.

ben: Quick Q — does this apply to Dedicated canaries too?

hao: Applies to hosted and dedicated control-plane-triggered canaries that touch the runtime. Dedicated serving pools operating on pinned GPUs are exempt from the concurrency cap, but coordinate if your canary hits shared control-plane services.

pm-alex: Why the change? Short answer: we've seen correlated scheduling spikes when >2 canaries hit the runtime in a single AZ during model kernel swaps. We want to avoid noisy neighbor effects.

ops-bot: Migration schedule (draft):
- 2025-03-10 01:00-05:00 UTC: ap-northeast-1 kernel migration (quiet window)
- 2025-03-12 02:00-06:00 UTC: eu-west-1 migration
- 2025-03-14 03:00-07:00 UTC: us-east-1 follow-up
Expect short quiet windows; non-urgent merges in affected regions should be postponed.

sylvia: Emergency/urgent release flow unchanged: label `urgent-hotfix` or `security-hotfix`, include smoke steps, and ping @oncall + me. We'll allocate a single prioritized canary slot. Use `--approvers sylvia,oncall`.

ben: Any CLI snippets for the new canary constraint? Would be helpful to gate locally.

hao: Small helper: `rw release start --canary-tag <tag> --region <region> --window 20m --concurrency 1` — deploys will be rejected by the gate if you exceed regional concurrency. Add `--override-freeze` only with explicit approvers.

pm-alex: Ops note: we'll surface the concurrency metric in the Release Console and add a warning banner when your planned canaries exceed the cap. ETA: 48h. Also adding a small FAQ to the release docs.

ops-bot: If a canary is failing and you need to abort quickly, commands:  `rw release abort --id <id>` then `kubectl rollout restart deployment/<svc> -n production` if you want a clean restart.

oncall: Acknowledged. I'll watch the migration windows and approve urgent labels. If you need fast approvals during maintenance, DM me with PR and smoke output.

ben: Noted, thanks. I'll adjust our scheduled canaries and update the sprint ticket.

sylvia: TL;DR: temporary regional canary cap = 2, upcoming kernel migration dates above, follow urgent-hotfix flow for emergencies, and ping this thread if you spot anything odd. :white_check_mark:
